subject: How to set up  strict invariance for categorical variables

messages.author: 96d9ff660a5feec3
messages.subject: How to set up  strict invariance for categorical variables
parts:
I am trying to run strict invariance for 4 items with 4-point Likert-scale between two groups.

In_MOV<-'inmov=~ST29Q01+ST29Q02+ST29Q04+ST29Q06'                                   ##In_MOV is measured by four items 
model_residuals<-cfa(In_MOV,data=re_PISA,group="CNT", ordered = c("ST29Q01","ST29Q02","ST29Q04","ST29Q06"),
                     group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds","residuals"))                                 ## add" residuals" into the group.equal line, but there is no effect on constraining on the parameters of residuals between two groups.

Because there is no effect on the parameters of residuals across groups (i.e. the parameters of residuals across groups are not constrained  equally), so I changed the codes based on previous posts.
But, the parameters of residuals are still not constrained equally. Could you please let me know how to run  strict invariance ? 

Here are codes: 
In_MOV_re<-'inmov=~ST29Q01+ST29Q02+ST29Q04+ST29Q06
                      ST29Q01 ~~ c(d1,d1)* ST29Q01
                      ST29Q02 ~~ c(d2,d2)* ST29Q02 
                      ST29Q04 ~~ c(d3,d3)*ST29Q04
                      ST29Q06 ~~ c(d4,d4)*ST29Q06'
model_residuals<-cfa(In_MOV_re,data=re_PISA,group="CNT", ordered = c("ST29Q01","ST29Q02","ST29Q04","ST29Q06"),
                     group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"))
summary(model_residuals)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How to set up  strict invariance for categorical variables
parts: But, the parameters of residuals are still not constrained equally. Could you please let me know how to run  strict invariance ?

The default in lavaan is parameterization = "delta", which identifies latent item-responses by fixing the total variances to 1.  Upon constraining thresholds, that identification constraint can be released in all but one group/occasion, so other total variances can be estimated.  But the delta parameterization does not allow you to do anything about residual variances because those are fixed relative to whatever the total variance is.

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

To instead fix the residual variances to 1 for identification in the configural model, use parameterization = "theta" (also described in the link above).  Then, when you constrain thresholds, the residual variances can be freely estimated in all but one group.  To test strict invariance, you cannot simply set estimates to be equal across groups because they are not estimated in the first group at all.  Because they are fixed to 1 in the first group for identification, you test strict invariance by fixing them to 1 in all groups.
